name: Côte Chalonnaise

known.via: English Wikipedia "Côte Chalonnaise" (a wine place on Wikidata)

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.

notes: Mercurey reds are noted for spicy cherry notes.
Montagny whites are noted for their acidity and body.
Bouzeron's Aligoté is light bodied with subtle spice, and is at its best within five years.

blurb.text: A Burgundy subregion south of the Côte d'Or, on rising ground above Chalon-sur-Saône. It has no Grand Cru vineyards. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay dominate, with some Aligoté and Gamay, and it includes Mercurey, Givry, Rully, Montagny and Bouzeron.
